model.rationale: A ten-point Democratic district, an incumbent seeking another term, and a cash advantage of roughly a thousand to one leave Galdo without a visible path; markets price Norcross near 96% and nothing in the record points to a closer race.
model.watch: Any independent polling showing a single-digit contest, or significant outside spending entering for the challenger, would be the first sign this is closer than it looks.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
This South Jersey district leans Democratic by about ten points, and incumbent Donald Norcross is running for another term. His Republican challenger, Damon Galdo, has run a minimal campaign, raising roughly sixteen thousand dollars against Norcross's one and a half million and entering the fall with about two thousand dollars on hand. Prediction markets put Norcross's chances near ninety-six percent, and no independent polls or expert ratings are available for the race.

The financial gap and the district's partisan lean make an upset unlikely. Norcross also carries the advantages of incumbency and established name recognition. The main source of uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves the exact margin unclear even though the direction of the outcome is not seriously in doubt.
